Nigerians have called on the Nigeria Football Federation to go for Pep Guardiola as Super Eagles coach after the Spaniard said his next job would be with a national team, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. Guardiola has been out of work since leaving Manchester City at the end of the 2025/2026 season, following a 10-year spell at the club. He cited fatigue as one of the reasons for leaving but made it clear that he is not done with coaching. In an interview with his former Barcelona teammate, Romario, on Romario TV, as reported by The Athletic, Guardiola was asked if there was a club he would like to manage. “A national team, which is my next step,” he replied. The comment has put several countries on alert, including Nigeria. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The Super Eagles are currently handled by Eric Chelle, but reports say any move for Guardiola would cost the NFF a lot of money. His appointment would also have to wait until June 2027 at the earliest, as the current NFF board does not have the power to award managerial contracts beyond May 2027. The United States are also reported to be interested and are favourites to land him after Mauricio Pochettino left their job for Manchester United. Former Nigeria international, Abiodun Obafemi, told PUNCH Sports Extra that the prospect of Guardiola in charge of the Super Eagles feels like a dream. Obafemi, a defender, was part of the Nigeria team that won gold at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta. Obafemi believes Guardiola’s quality as a coach would transform the natural talent in the Nigerian squad, although he admits it will be hard for the dream to come true. “Honestly, that feels like a dream. It really does. I think he’s a very good coach and I know if we are lucky and are able to get him, he’s going to transform the natural talent our boys have,” Obafemi said. We have so many talents, and there will be hope for the upcoming boys. I know it is a dream, but if he says yes to us if we go for him, it will be a dream come true.” Fans on X also reacted to the news positively, with some even offering to pay his salary. Zaharaddeen Kallah (@zikallah) wrote, “If Nigerian supporters can afford to contribute to his salary, we can expect him.” Deepee (@dpXmaki) said, “A country can dream.” Others raised doubts over the environment he would find. @YahBuchi wrote, “Nigeria will go far, but a toxic environment may not allow him to stay because they won’t allow him to go around and select as he wishes. With Pep, externals like (Victor) Osimhen may not get a call-up. Quality local bleeds will run the show.” Okorie Dani said, “The Nigeria @NGSuperEagles is having the same issues as Manchester United football club. It’s an eternal challenge that has nothing to do with the players or the coaches at all. So if we hire Pep, the problem will still be there. Except we make a change. Thanks.” @BiGFargiN backed the idea with a quote attributed to Chinua Achebe, “Let the young man go out and hunt. If he kills the elephant, his poverty ends; if the elephant kills him, his poverty still ends. Chinua Achebe. It’s a win-win situation for me.” Italy has also tried to land Guardiola before. He revealed that he turned down the four-time world champions because it was not the right time to return to management after 18 years of working every day. He said he even felt ashamed to say no to a country like Italy and that he would probably have accepted had they come one or two years later.
